title: Five ways to view a robot in Rerun
brief: One read-only Rerun viewer per robot description: 3D on the left; every actuator's command vs state, every sensor's measurement and every part's configuration; composed from the description tree so the pendulum, the UR5e and the dual-arm cell come out of the same function.
boundary: Real Rerun 0.40 recordings and blueprints, opened in the stock web viewer. Simulated: commands are a real UR5e trajectory, states are it delayed 90 ms with sag and noise (the pendulum runs a PD loop); camera frames are a pinhole render of the same geometry; temperatures, the 2.6 s elbow fault and all configs are sample numbers. Not registered as dashboards.
invariants: Same recording for all five (same entities, samples, colours); only the blueprint differs
Same three robots: 1-DOF pendulum + side camera, UR5e + wrist camera, dual-arm cell (two UR5e subtrees, each with its wrist camera) + overhead camera
Stills at 1440×900, dark theme, playhead at t = 5.0 s
Read-only: no command path, no bus

media.html:
def v1_tabs_by_type(robot: str, scene: Scene, tab: int = 0, sub_tab: int = 0) -> rrb.Blueprint:
    """V1 Zach's sketch: Servos / Cameras / Config. Servos grouped by the subtree they hang off."""
    root = ROBOTS[robot]
    groups = []
    for group, servos in servo_groups(root):
        cells = [_position_plot(p, f"{p.split('/')[-1]} · ° cmd ··· state —") for p, _ in servos]
        cells.append(_overlay(f"{group} · temperature °C", [p for p, _ in servos], ["temperature"], legend=False))
        groups.append(rrb.Grid(*cells, grid_columns=min(4, len(cells)), name=group))
    # WHY sub-tabs per subtree: Zach, "on servos you can break down by right arm etc so you don't have a crazy huge list"
    servos_tab = rrb.Tabs(*groups, name="Servos", active_tab=sub_tab) if len(groups) > 1 else rrb.Vertical(groups[0], name="Servos")
    cams = [_camera_view(p) for p, _ in cameras_of(root)]
    cameras_tab = rrb.Grid(*cams, grid_columns=min(2, len(cams)), name="Cameras")
    config_tab = rrb.Vertical(*[rrb.TextDocumentView(origin=f"/config/{d}", name=f"{d} · config")
                                for d in config_docs(root)], name="Config")  # fmt: skip
    return _frame(robot, scene, rrb.Tabs(servos_tab, cameras_tab, config_tab, active_tab=tab))

fr1.evidence: One joint per plot, ~330 px tall; the right elbow's flat state vs moving command is obvious (sub-tab still). Only one arm visible at a time.

fr2.evidence: Plots, sub-tabs, cameras and config tables are all derived from the tree; but the tab set is a fixed type list, so a new part kind needs a new tab.

fr3.evidence: Pendulum: 1 plot; dual-arm: 2 sub-tabs × 7 plots. No long list, but a 4-arm cell means 4 sub-tabs.

fr4.evidence: Cameras get a whole tab, large and legible, but are never seen with the servos; only frustums show in 3D.

fr5.evidence: Config tab: a full table per group (bus/id, kp, kd, max A, limits) plus cameras, fully readable.

g1.evidence: The builder only logs to an .rrd; there is no command path and no transport is imported or opened.

g2.evidence: All 15 recordings (and the tab variants) loaded in the stock Rerun 0.40 web viewer from the saved .rrd with their blueprint, 0 viewer errors, no panic.

g3.evidence: Every blueprint is _frame(): Horizontal(Spatial3DView, …) with the 3D first; seen in every still.

media.html:
def _stock_servo(path: str, part: Part) -> rrb.Container:
    return rrb.Vertical(_position_plot(path, f"{path.split('/')[-1]} · ° cmd ··· state —"), _config_view(path),
                        row_shares=[1.5, 1], name=path)  # fmt: skip
def _stock_camera(path: str, part: Part) -> rrb.Container:
    return rrb.Vertical(_camera_view(path), _config_view(path), row_shares=[2.2, 1], name=path)
def _stock_group(path: str, part: Part) -> rrb.Container:
    kids = [stock_view(f"{path}/{c.name}" if path else c.name, c) for c in part.children]
    return rrb.Grid(*kids, grid_columns=math.ceil(math.sqrt(len(kids))) if len(kids) > 3 else len(kids), name=path)
STOCK_VIEWS: dict[str, Callable[[str, Part], rrb.Container]] = {
    "servo": _stock_servo, "camera": _stock_camera, "group": _stock_group}  # fmt: skip
def stock_view(path: str, part: Part) -> rrb.Container:
    return STOCK_VIEWS[part.kind](path, part)
def v2_tabs_mirror_tree(robot: str, scene: Scene, tab: int = 0) -> rrb.Blueprint:
    """V2: one tab per top-level part; each tab is that part's stock view, composed recursively from its children."""
    root = ROBOTS[robot]
    return _frame(robot, scene, rrb.Tabs(*[stock_view(c.name, c) for c in root.children], active_tab=tab))

fr1.evidence: Per-joint plots but ~150 px tall, sharing the tab with config cards; cmd/state separation readable, smaller than V1.

fr2.evidence: The layout is STOCK_VIEWS recursion over the tree: the pendulum, the arm and the cell all came out of it with no per-robot code; a new kind is one registry line.

fr3.evidence: Dual-arm: 3 tabs, 7 cards each. Deep trees nest grids, which will get small past two levels.

fr4.evidence: Each wrist camera sits beside its own arm's joints; the overhead camera is its own tab (not seen with the arms).

fr5.evidence: A config card per part, right next to its plot, but cut to two lines at 1440×900; the full table needs a maximise.

def v3_tview(robot: str, scene: Scene, tab: int = 0) -> rrb.Blueprint:
    """V3: one read-only page like moteus tview: the live table first, camera thumbnails, two summary plots."""
    root = ROBOTS[robot]
    servos = [p for p, _ in servos_of(root)]
    cams = [_camera_view(p) for p, _ in cameras_of(root)]
    right = rrb.Vertical(
        rrb.TextDocumentView(origin="/now", name="now · every servo and camera at the playhead"),
        rrb.Horizontal(*cams, name="cameras"),
        rrb.Horizontal(_overlay("tracking error ° (cmd − state), every servo", servos, ["position/error"], False),
                       _overlay("temperature °C, every servo", servos, ["temperature"], False)),
        row_shares=[4.6, 1.1, 1.0],
    )  # fmt: skip
    return _frame(robot, scene, right)

fr3.evidence: Dual-arm (12 servos) already pushes right_arm's last row below the fold; a bigger cell is a scrolling list, the thing Zach wanted to avoid.

fr4.evidence: All camera feeds always visible beside the numbers, as thumbnails (~220 px).

fr5.evidence: Config is a table under the live one, in the same scroll; readable but out of sight on the dual-arm cell.

def v4_tabs_by_signal(robot: str, scene: Scene, tab: int = 0) -> rrb.Blueprint:
    """V4: a tab per signal; in each, one plot per subtree overlays all its joints, command dots vs state lines."""
    root = ROBOTS[robot]
    groups = servo_groups(root)

    def per_group(signal: str, unit: str) -> rrb.Vertical:
        return rrb.Vertical(*[_overlay(f"{g} · {signal} {unit} · cmd ··· state — · {_key(s)}", [p for p, _ in s],
                                       [f"{signal}/cmd", f"{signal}/state"], legend=False) for g, s in groups],
                            name=signal.title())  # fmt: skip

    health = rrb.Vertical(*[rrb.Horizontal(
        _overlay(f"{g} · tracking error ° · {_key(s)}", [p for p, _ in s], ["position/error"], legend=False),
        _overlay(f"{g} · temperature °C", [p for p, _ in s], ["temperature"], legend=False),
        _overlay(f"{g} · fault code", [p for p, _ in s], ["fault"], legend=False),
        column_shares=[1.3, 1, 0.8]) for g, s in groups], name="Health")  # fmt: skip
    cams = [_camera_view(p) for p, _ in cameras_of(root)]
    config = rrb.Vertical(*[rrb.TextDocumentView(origin=f"/config/{d}", name=f"{d} · config")
                            for d in config_docs(root)], name="Config")  # fmt: skip
    return _frame(robot, scene, rrb.Tabs(per_group("position", "°"), per_group("velocity", "°/s"),
                                         per_group("effort", "N·m"), health,
                                         rrb.Grid(*cams, grid_columns=min(2, len(cams)), name="Cameras"), config,
                                         active_tab=tab))  # fmt: skip

fr1.evidence: Both arms visible together, but six joints per plot: the elbow's divergence reads, a single joint's lag needs the colour key or hover.

fr2.evidence: Per-subtree plots come from the tree; the six signal tabs are fixed, so a camera-only or IMU subtree has no natural place.

fr3.evidence: One plot per subtree per signal whatever the joint count: dual-arm is two plots per tab; more arms just add rows.

fr4.evidence: Cameras live in their own tab, apart from the signals.

fr5.evidence: Config tab: the same full per-group tables as V1.

g1.evidence: The builder only logs to an .rrd; there is no command path and no transport is imported or opened.

g2.evidence: All 15 recordings (and the tab variants) loaded in the stock Rerun 0.40 web viewer from the saved .rrd with their blueprint, 0 viewer errors, no panic.

g3.evidence: Every blueprint is _frame(): Horizontal(Spatial3DView, …) with the 3D first; seen in every still.

def _card(path: str, part: Part, depth: int) -> rrb.Container:
    if part.kind == "servo":
        return rrb.Horizontal(_position_plot(path, f"{path.split('/')[-1]} · ° cmd ··· state —"),
                              _config_view(path, "config"), column_shares=[2, 1.3], name=path)  # fmt: skip
    if part.kind == "camera":
        return rrb.Vertical(_camera_view(path), _config_view(path, "config"), row_shares=[2, 1], name=path)
    kids = [_card(f"{path}/{c.name}" if path else c.name, c, depth + 1) for c in part.children]
    box = rrb.Horizontal if depth % 2 == 0 else rrb.Vertical
    return box(*kids, name=path or part.name)
def v5_cards(robot: str, scene: Scene, tab: int = 0) -> rrb.Blueprint:
    """V5: every part a card (plot + config, or image + config), nested to mirror the tree, all visible at once."""
    return _frame(robot, scene, _card("", ROBOTS[robot], 0))

fr1.evidence: On the dual-arm cell each plot is ~60 px tall: command and state overlap into one line except the faulted elbow.

fr2.evidence: Pure recursion over the tree; a new part is a new card with no edit.

fr3.evidence: The opposite of 'no huge list': every part is on screen, so the dual-arm cell already crushes the cards.

fr4.evidence: All cameras always visible, but the wrist cameras are thumbnails in a crowded column.

fr5.evidence: Config is beside every plot but truncated to its first line at this size.

g1.evidence: The builder only logs to an .rrd; there is no command path and no transport is imported or opened.

g2.evidence: All 15 recordings (and the tab variants) loaded in the stock Rerun 0.40 web viewer from the saved .rrd with their blueprint, 0 viewer errors, no panic.

g3.evidence: Every blueprint is _frame(): Horizontal(Spatial3DView, …) with the 3D first; seen in every still.

hardGates.why: A viewer that can command is not a viewer; it never opens a bus.

defaultWhy: Tabs by part type (80) and Tabs mirror the tree (77) are co-leaders, 3 points apart, so the pick is fragile. V1 wins on big per-joint plots and a complete Config tab; V2 wins on composition (the layout is a registry + recursion) and on keeping each wrist camera with its arm.
decisionHinge: How much FR2 (composition) outweighs FR5 (config readability). Move 10 points from FR5 to FR2 and V2 leads 81 to 78. A splice probably beats both: V2's registry and tree tabs, with V1's bigger per-joint plots and a Config tab (or V3's now-table) as the stock view of a group.
